1	# Entire for Orca
2	
3	![An orca in an Entire T-shirt splashes beside the words Entire for Orca ADE: bring the power of Entire into Orca ADE, with trails, findings and checkpoints. Marked unofficial.](images/banner.jpg)
4	
5	An [Orca](https://onorca.dev) plugin that shows [Entire](https://entire.com) trails, findings and checkpoints
6	for the workspace you're working in, in a panel beside your terminals. It gives Entire the place in Orca
7	that GitHub pull requests and checks already have.
8	
9	It's a community plugin, and it only reads: it never creates, approves or changes anything in Entire.
10	
11	## What you get
12	
13	**The Entire panel** (the layers icon in the right sidebar) follows the focused workspace and shows:
14	
15	- the repo's Entire status and any active agent sessions
16	- the branch's trail: its change, the code review, the merge gates (approvals, checks, findings, up to
17	  date) and the findings, each of which you can copy, one at a time or all together
18	- the branch's recent checkpoints
19	- a connection check that says what worked and what didn't
20	
21	It reads Entire when you switch workspaces or branches, when an agent finishes, and every 5 minutes.
22	↻ reads it now.
23	
24	**Commands** in the command palette:
25	
26	- **Entire: Check connection** runs the same check and reports it as a notification.
27	- **Entire: Refresh panel** reads Entire for the focused workspace now.
28	
29	## Requirements
30	
31	- **Orca 1.4.246 or later.**
32	- **The Entire CLI, installed and logged in where your repos live:**
33	  - Repos on this computer: Entire on the PATH Orca starts with.
34	  - Repos in WSL: Entire inside that WSL distro, logged in there. The plugin runs it through `wsl.exe`
35	    in a login shell, so `~/.local/bin` counts.
36	  - Repos on a paired Orca server: Entire on this computer, logged in to an account that can see the
37	    repository, for the trail and findings. For status and checkpoints, the plugin also needs SSH to the
38	    server (see [Paired servers](#paired-servers)).
39	- **Entire enabled in the repo** (`entire enable`) for its status and checkpoints. A repo without it
40	  still shows its trail.
41	- **Restart Orca after installing Entire**, so the plugin sees it on PATH.
42	
43	## Install
44	
45	Turn on plugins in **Settings → Plugins** if they're off. Then open the plugin in Orca's community
46	catalog, <https://onorca.dev/plugins/petercr.entire?catalog=community>, and install it. Orca shows
47	what the plugin asks for before you approve it:
48	
49	- **Workspace (read):** which workspace is focused, its branch and its terminals, to know which repo to
50	  read.
51	- **Notifications:** for **Entire: Check connection** and for problems found by **Entire: Refresh
52	  panel**.
53	- **Agents (read):** to read Entire again when an agent finishes.
54	
55	Then open the **Entire** panel.
56	
57	## Platforms
58	
59	| Where the workspace is | Status                                                                       |
60	| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
61	| Windows                | Tested                                                                       |
62	| WSL, from Windows      | Tested                                                                       |
63	| A paired Orca server   | Tested from Windows. Status and checkpoints over SSH work on Windows only.   |
64	| macOS, Linux           | Not tested. Finding the workspace expects Orca's CLI where Windows has it, so it may fail; reports welcome. |
65	
66	## Paired servers
67	
68	Orca tells plugins only the repo name of a workspace on a paired server, with no branch or path. The
69	plugin finds it in the server's worktree list, then:
70	
71	- reads the trail and findings with this computer's Entire, by the repo's origin URL and branch;
72	- reads status, checkpoints and the diff size over SSH to the server, using the address Orca saved
73	  for it. SSH runs with `BatchMode`, so it can't ask for a passphrase: add the key to the ssh-agent
74	  (`ssh-add`) first.
75	
76	If the plugin can't reach the server, the panel shows the trail and findings and says why the rest is
77	missing. Two worktrees of one repo on the same server look alike to plugins, and the panel says so.
78	
79	## What it runs and reads
80	
81	The plugin runs everything from Orca's plugin worker on this computer, as you:
82	
83	- `entire`: `--version`, `status`, `trail show`, `trail finding list` and `checkpoint list`, all
84	  read-only, with `--json`. It sets `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1`, so these background reads send Entire
85	  no usage analytics.
86	- `git diff --shortstat` against the trail's base branch, for the line counts.
87	- Orca's own CLI (`terminal show`, `worktree list`, `repo list`, `environment show`), to find the
88	  focused workspace's path.
89	- `wsl.exe` for WSL workspaces, and `ssh` for paired servers.
90	- On Windows, for paired servers only: the saved SSH targets in Orca's profile database
91	  (`%APPDATA%\orca\profiles\<profile>\profile-state.db`), opened read-only.
92	
93	It keeps what it reads in memory for the last 10 workspaces and stores nothing on disk. The panel
94	itself has no network access. Text from Entire, such as finding bodies, is shown as text and never
95	run.
96	
97	## Troubleshooting
98	
99	- **"Open a terminal in it and try again":** without a terminal, the plugin knows a workspace only by
100	  its name and branch, and many repos share `main`. A terminal in the workspace tells it which one.
101	- **Entire not found, or an old version:** restart Orca after installing or updating Entire.
102	- **"SSH to … failed" on a paired server:** add the server's key to the ssh-agent with `ssh-add`.
103	- **"repository not on Entire for this computer's login":** log this computer's Entire in to an
104	  account that can see the repository.
105	- **More detail:** run **Entire: Check connection**, or open the plugin's **Logs** in **Settings →
106	  Plugins**. Each read writes its report there.
107	
108	## Develop
109	
110	No build step: the worker is plain ES modules under `src/worker`, and the panel is `panel/index.html`.
111	
112	```sh
113	node --test
114	```
115	
116	To run a working copy in Orca, open **Settings → Plugins**, choose **Development folders…** from the
117	**⋯** menu, add this folder, then review and enable **Entire**. Orca runs the folder in place and
118	reloads it when its files change. After editing the worker, turn the plugin off and on so the panel's
119	next request starts a fresh worker.
120	
121	To run the worker inside Orca's own runtime without the GUI (Windows, Orca installed):
122	
123	```sh
124	node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs no-terminal
125	```
126	
127	From WSL, run it with Windows Node (`node.exe`, or its full path under `/mnt/c` when Windows is not on
128	WSL's PATH) from the repo's `/mnt/c/...` path.
129	
130	The plan, the limits of Orca's plugin API it works within, and the spike results are in
131	[docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).
132	
133	## License
134	
135	[MIT](LICENSE)

22	## What Orca's plugin API allows (1.4.245, updated for 1.4.250)
23	
24	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
25	
26	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
27	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
28	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
29	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
30	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
31	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
32	  `settings.*` (worker only).
33	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
34	- The command palette ignores a command's return value. The Run button in Settings → Plugins shows its
35	  first 200 characters in a toast. Worker stdout and stderr go to the plugin's Logs (last 200 lines).
36	- Panels are sealed: no network, no browser permissions (so no async Clipboard API;
37	  `execCommand('copy')` in a click works), links only through `orca.shell.openExternal` (1.1).
38	- Host API 1.2 (Orca 1.4.246) added the panel channel: a panel calls `orca.plugin.request(name,
39	  input, { timeoutMs })`, which starts the worker if needed and runs the handler it registered with
40	  `orca.panels.handle`; the worker posts with `orca.panels.post` (fire and forget, 256 KiB) and the
41	  panel listens with `orca.plugin.on`. Answers go up to 1 MiB, requests up to 120 s. A panel also
42	  hears `workspace.changed` and agent events with `orca.on`. 1.2 also brought `agents.list`; 1.3
43	  brings `workspace.list` (every workspace with its path and host, worker only), which could replace
44	  much of `src/worker/workspace.mjs` once the installed Orca offers it.
45	- Before 1.2 the panel worked only from a development folder: the worker wrote its data into the
46	  panel file (installed copies are hash-checked), and ↻ reached the worker through Orca's audit log.
47	  Both stopgaps are gone (branch `panel-channel`).
48	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
49	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
50	- 1.4.250 has the `orca plugin` CLI: `validate`, `inspect` (content hash), `release-entry`, `logs`,
51	  and `dev request` to call a panel handler. Load the plugin through Settings → Plugins →
52	  Development folders.
53	- `publisher` is deprecated: Orca names the publisher after the repository owner for catalog and Git
54	  installs (`petercr.entire`) and `local` for a folder (`local.entire`). Leaving it out needs
55	  `>=1.4.246`. Ids may not start with `orca-`.

Every call is checked against the capabilities the user approved, and params are validated before Orca runs anything: params are strict, so a field this Orca does not know is refused with `invalid_params` instead of being dropped. Mutations are recorded in the audit log as `plugin:<publisher>.<id>`.

Methods whose capability is `none` need no capability but still need the plugin enabled and approved. `shell.openExternal` and `files.saveAs` also need transient user activation (a click or key press in the calling frame, within a few seconds), are rate-limited, and run only in the desktop app; frames also reach them as `orca.shell.openExternal(url)` and `orca.files.saveAs({ suggestedName, mimeType, data })`, which resolves with `{ status: "saved" }`, or `{ status: "cancelled" }` when the person cancels the dialog. Saved files carry the OS mark for downloaded files.

## Methods

| Method | Capability | Surfaces | Mutation | Since | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`workspace.readContext`](#workspacereadcontext) | `workspace:read` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.0 | Id, branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused. |
-----
| [`secrets.protection`](#secretsprotection) | `secrets:own` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.1 | How secrets are protected at rest: `os-keyring`, or `unavailable` (no OS key store, or Linux `basic_text`), where `secrets.set` fails. |
| [`settings.get`](#settingsget) | `settings:own` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.0 | Reads every setting the plugin owns. |
| [`settings.set`](#settingsset) | `settings:own` | worker, panel, editor | yes | 1.0 | Writes one setting the plugin owns. |
| [`shell.openExternal`](#shellopenexternal) | none | panel, editor | no | 1.1 | Opens an http:, https: or mailto: URL in the default browser. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only. Orca asks the person before an http(s) host the plugin was not allowed; `opened` is false if they cancel. |
| [`files.saveAs`](#filessaveas) | none | panel, editor | yes | 1.1 | Offers data (a string or ArrayBuffer, up to 64 MiB) in Orca's save dialog; the plugin never learns the path. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only. |
| [`plugin.request`](#pluginrequest) | none | panel, editor | no | 1.2 | Asks the plugin's own worker to run the handler it registered with `orca.panels.handle(name)`, starting the worker if needed; resolves with what the handler returned. `unknown_method` when no handler has that name. |
| [`agents.list`](#agentslist) | `agent:read` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.2 (`workspaceId`: 1.10) | The agents in the focused workspace, or in the one `workspaceId` names (rejected when no workspace has it): their terminal, title, agent kind, status, session and dispatched task. `agent.status.changed` reports each change after. |
| [`events.subscribe`](#eventssubscribe) | none | panel, editor | no | 1.2 | Delivers a workspace, agent or editor event to this panel as `orca.on(event)`; needs the event's read capability, when it has one. The frame APIs call it for you. |
| [`statusBar.update`](#statusbarupdate) | none | worker | no | 1.2 | Changes one of the plugin's `contributes.statusBarItems` (named by `id`): fields given replace their current value, `visible: false` hides it. Desktop app only; lasts until Orca restarts, and is hidden while the plugin is disabled. A plugin with `main` and status bar items has its worker started when it is enabled and kept running while it stays enabled, so a worker can poll and update its items without an event or a hook. |
| [`appearance.read`](#appearanceread) | `appearance:write` | worker | no | 1.4 | Reads the current desktop appearance revision for a conditional update. |

content.text:
I've added a **Report a problem on GitHub** button to the panel and two issue templates. They're on a new branch, `report-issue`, and not committed yet. The unit tests pass (61) and `orca plugin validate .` accepts the plugin. I haven't clicked the button in Orca itself.

**The button** ([panel/index.html](/C:/Users/pcruc/Web%20Projects/orca-entire-extension/panel/index.html)):
- It sits at the bottom of the panel, so it shows in every state, including errors and "no workspace focused". It opens the link with `orca.shell.openExternal`, which is the only way Orca lets a panel open a link. Orca asks the user once before opening a site the plugin hasn't been allowed. If the link can't open, the button says "Couldn't open GitHub" for a few seconds.
- It opens a new issue from the bug report form, with its Environment field already filled in. The panel can see the plugin version, Orca's plugin API version, the OS, the Entire CLI version and whether the workspace is local, in WSL or on a paired server, so those go in. No paths, repo names or branches. Nothing is sent until the user submits the issue on GitHub.
- The panel can't read the plugin version from Orca, so it keeps its own copy in `PLUGIN_VERSION`. A new test fails if it ever differs from the manifest's version, so it has to change with each release. Another test checks that the link never contains the workspace's path, repo name or branch.

**Templates** (in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`):
- [bug_report.yml](/C:/Users/pcruc/Web%20Projects/orca-entire-extension/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what happened, what was expected, steps to reproduce, where the workspace is, the Orca version (the panel can't see it), the environment and the connection report. It reminds people that issues are public and to remove repo names, paths and finding text. It also points problems with Entire or Orca themselves to those projects.
- [feature_request.yml](/C:/Users/pcruc/Web%20Projects/orca-entire-extension/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml) is a short form for ideas. I added it as an extra.

I also updated the README (the button, what its link contains, and a troubleshooting line) and added a note about `PLUGIN_VERSION` and the form's field id to CLAUDE.md.

GitHub only uses issue forms that are on `main`. Until this is merged, the button opens a blank issue and the environment details are lost.

To try it, turn the plugin off and on in Settings → Plugins and click the button. Want me to commit this and open a PR?
ok great it works and open github to file a new issue. BUT we didn't add any kind of issue template to help the user

We did add the templates, but GitHub hasn't picked them up yet. GitHub only reads issue templates from the repo's default branch (`main`). Ours exist only on your local, uncommitted `report-issue` branch. So the link's `?template=bug_report.yml` points to a form GitHub can't find, and it falls back to a blank issue.

Once the templates are merged into `main`, the same button will open the **Report a problem** form with the Environment field filled in. Nothing in the panel needs to change.

Two ways to get there:

1. **Commit and open a PR** for the whole branch (button, templates, tests and docs). The form works as soon as you merge it. This is the simplest option.
2. **Merge the templates first** in their own small PR. The form then goes live right away for anyone filing issues, and the button follows in a later PR.

Want me to commit and open the PR (option 1)?
